text: Why can the same visible text compare as unequal?
choices: Java compares strings by memory address
Accented characters are always unequal to themselves
é can be one code point or an e followed by a combining accent, and the sequences differ
The comparison depends on the display font
explanation: equals compares code point sequences, and both forms are legitimate. Normalize with NFC before comparing text that came from outside — usernames, filenames, search terms — and do it once at the boundary rather than remembering at every comparison.
